scope.question: Can a concentration-guided one-pair query select a useful local certificate without examining all overlaps or the full allowed set?
scope.status: Known-control diagnostic; general arguments remain HYPOTHESIS/proof candidates; no novelty claim
scope.input_contract: A prescribed three-speed core plus four distinct positive residual speeds; core selection itself is not solved. All frozen full speed lists have gcd1 and retain the original unit period.
selection_rule: Construct the complete closed safe set of only the supplied core on [0,1], retaining singleton components and counting construction cost.
Among positive-length core components select the widest, breaking ties by smallest left endpoint. Never change this window after seeing residual data.
Compute the four individual blocking durations D on the selected window using endpoint primitives; E=sum(D)-window_length.
Rank the six pairs by descending min(D_i,D_j), then ascending numerical speed pair. This is an overlap upper cap, not a prediction or lower bound.
If E<0, certify positive duration from singles and make no overlap query. Otherwise if the largest cap is at most E, record that no one-pair bound can be positive and make no overlap query.
Otherwise query exactly the first ranked pair's overlap O and use lower bound O-E. Never rerank or query another pair after failure.

If no positive duration certificate resulted, test only the selected window's right endpoint against all seven nonreference speeds. If valid, record its shared safe-lap intersection and equality directions to distinguish a positive local interval from an isolated contact. If invalid, return uncertified and stop the ordered diagnostic campaign. Do not select a second endpoint or window.
scope.overlap_evaluator: After selecting a<b, choose h in {1,2} minimizing (abs(b-h*a),h); put r=b-h*a. Use signed-residual phase strips and the exact periodic endpoint primitive. Count all strips and primitive calls. This is an evaluation choice, not a pair-ranking score. The independent verifier uses direct blocking-interval intersection instead.
validation_contract: Exact rational arithmetic only; no time/phase grid or broad speed search.
Primary generator must not read full allowed sets, all-pair archives, benchmark durations, or the independent implementation.

Independent verifier may read schema/output/protocol but must not read/import primary implementation. Use a separately structured core event partition, direct chosen-pair interval intersections, and endpoint substitution.
Compare policy outputs afterward to already archived local actual durations and best-pair/tree bounds. Benchmark sources do not feed selection. No new full seven-runner safe-set reconstruction.
These are known controls informed by prior research, not blind or held-out validation. Preserve the first uncertified result without retuning.
scope.cost_contract: Count core laps/events/components, four single-duration primitive calls at two endpoints each, six scalar pair caps, at most one exact overlap evaluation with all residual-strip construction and primitive calls, and at most one seven-runner endpoint plus its safe-lap intersection. Report rational operand bit sizes separately. No uniform or empirical runtime speedup claim follows merely from the one-query count.
scope.scope_limits: No arbitrary-speed existence guarantee, no core-selection theorem, no complete strictness classification, no external proof certification or novelty assertion. A failed policy is not failed loneliness. +7/+9 and cutoff polishing remain parked.

verification.agreement: All semantic records/digests, evaluation certificates, and declared cost counters
verification.independence: Primary core safe-lap intersections/signed-residual endpoint primitive versus core threshold-event states/direct chosen-pair interval intersections. Verifier did not read/import primary implementation, benchmark archives, unselected overlaps, or full seven-runner safe sets.
verification.post_selection_benchmark_checks: Five baseline archive hashes, source scalar pointers and six selected-window/excess matches checked separately after policy selection; benchmark sources never feed generator or independent verifier.

cost_limits: Counts include repeated core construction without caching. Primitive/reported operand bit sizes are per-case, not bounds on every transient operation. No timing benchmark, general constant-operation guarantee, or runtime speedup claim.
supplied_general_arguments: Every one-pair score is at most C-E, where C is the second-largest single duration. C<=E rejects the entire one-pair certificate class on that window before querying overlaps.
C>E is only capacity, not guaranteed realized overlap. The marginal cap is sharp for abstract measurable events, not asserted realizable by runner speeds.
For selected a<b and h1or2, signed-residual affine strips have positive endpoint frequencies a and b/h; the periodic primitive evaluates exact overlap using O(1+|b-ha||J|) strip candidates.
important_limits: Known controls informed design; not blind or held-out evidence. No new common-start existence coverage or core-selection theorem.

The frozen policy fails on strict16 although its selected window contains duration1/896. The old best-pair and best-tree bounds there are negative, and a prior abstract cover preserves all single/pair totals.
No observed selected-pair failure is repairable by choosing another pair on the same selected window. Conditional cap-ranking sufficiency remains undecided by this batch.
No singles-positive exit or r0 overlap evaluator is exercised. Negative-r evaluation is exercised twice.
First uncertified case is the last prescribed input, so stop-rule enforcement yields no measured early-stop savings.
Endpoint rescues are separate certificate paths; unqueried overlap is null, not zero. Positive shared safe-lap interval is distinct from an isolated contact.

Exact finite checks OBSERVED/REPRODUCED. General implications remain HYPOTHESIS/proof candidates; no independent human proof certification, formal proof-assistant verification, novelty assertion, or general LRC proof.
next_proposed_not_run: With an explicit larger input/cost contract, derive a condition selecting added speed geometry or a quantitative intersection bound that excludes every summary-compatible complete-cover arrangement. Use archived strict16,112,tight controls and prior sparse/alternative-window rules as comparison targets; no fitted reranking, new scan, cutoff polishing, or+7/+9 extension.
dependency_policy: Two standard-library scripts. Primary reads protocol, self hash and its archive in check mode. Verifier reads protocol/results and its archive, never primary code or historical benchmark archives. Proof-context and benchmark sources are recorded separately.
